articles.title: Tiafoe completes epic comeback to break Michelsen’s heart at US Open
articles.summary: No 11 seed rallies for 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (6) win. Tiafoe into third US Open semi-final in five years. American will play Alcaraz or Shelton in last four. At the end of more than four and a half hours of escalating drama inside the world’s biggest tennis stadium, a devastated Alex Michelsen…
body: Only a couple of hours earlier, the 28-year-old Tiafoe had been two sets down and two points from elimination in the third set, with Michelsen seemingly bound for the biggest victory of his young career. Instead, Tiafoe roared back from the brink to win a quarter-final that will be long remembered in New York, defeating Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (6) on Tuesday afternoon to reach the last four at Flushing Meadows for the third time in five years. He will face either Carlos Alcaraz or Ben Shelton on Friday for a place in his first grand slam final.

The contest unfolded inside a half-empty Arthur Ashe Stadium amid an oddly subdued atmosphere for an all-American quarter-final, with many spectators taking a break after Aryna Sabalenka ’s grueling three-set win over Linda Noskova in the day’s opener. The setting was hardly ideal for the 11th-seeded Tiafoe, who had played all four previous rounds in the more intimate cauldron of Louis Armstrong Stadium next door, where he thrives on the crowd’s energy and has yet to lose in 10 career matches.

articles.title: LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection as it looks to ‘begin the next chapter’
articles.summary: Saudi investors stopped backing LIV this year. Rahm, DeChambeau and Smith among the creditors. LIV Golf, the breakaway tour that spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the PGA and triggered bitter divisions within the sport, has filed for bankruptcy protection in the US.
body: The filing at a New Jersey court indicates LIV, which abruptly lost its deep-pocketed Saudi investors earlier this year, intends to restructure and return in a new form.
But documents show LIV owes between $500m and $1bn in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players like Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Cam Smith.

The future of those popular players remains deeply unclear; they are now faced with deciding whether to remain with the tour in its new guise, or leave and attempt to pursue the millions of dollars they are owed in court.

“This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf,” said the chief executive, Scott O’Neil, whose organisation had already laid off the majority of its staff this month.

articles.summary: Ayyoub Bouaddi belies his age with a mature Champions League performance on his first Manchester City start to showcase why the club were so intent on signing the 18-year-old.
body: The midfielder took centre stage for Morocco at this summer's World Cup and City spent £86m to sign him from Lille, making him the most expensive teenager in Premier League history.
And after two substitute appearances for City, he was handed his first start against Porto and did not look out of place during the 2-0 victory.

Erling Haaland will take the plaudits for his two goals, but it was Bouaddi who caught the eye with a tidy and assured performance in the middle of the park, signalling early signs that Rodri may not be too sorely missed after his departure.
"His age, his game – he looks absolutely born to do it," former Chelsea winger Pat Nevin said on BBC Radio 5 Live during the game.

articles.summary: Sometimes football is silly, sometimes it doesn’t make much sense, and sometimes it’s fun for it. On a night when there were 37 shots and the goalkeepers shared 13 occasionally absurd saves between them, José Mourinho’s current side beat his former team Inter on his Champions League return to Real…

You might be tempted to say the Italians had shot themselves in the foot, only if they tried Courtois would probably save that too. “If he wasn’t voted man of the match tonight, he never will be,” Mourinho said. It took 77 minutes for him to be beaten, Carlos Augusto’s goal giving this match a frantic last 15 minutes and Inter hope of justice, but it didn’t happen again. So a game that could have had any scoreline – “5-1 to us, 6-6, I don’t want to say they could have won,” Mourinho suggested – actually ended 2-1. articles.title: Frances Tiafoe Speaks Out on Alex Michelsen Sobbing Uncontrollably in His Arms After Painful US Open Loss
articles.summary: Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen’s thrilling all-American battle in the quarterfinals of the 2026 US Open ended in emotional scenes, as Michelsen bared his devastation over his difficult loss.
body: After losing the first two sets, Tiafoe found himself on the brink of defeat in the quarterfinals of the US Open, as Michelsen served for the match at 5-4 in the third. However, the 22-year-old faltered under the pressure, serving two double faults and handing Tiafoe the opening he needed to kick off his remarkable comeback.

The world No. 12 seized the opportunity, winning the third set before carrying his momentum into the fourth to force a decider. Although Michelsen raced to a 3-0 lead in the fifth set, Tiafoe battled back strongly to secure a 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6(10-6) victory after a 4-hour, 38-minute contest.

Immediately after sealing his hard-fought victory, Tiafoe cut his celebrations short to rush over and embrace Michelsen, who broke down in tears and sobbed inconsolably in the 28-year-old’s arms after letting the match slip away.

Having experienced the pain of brutal five-set losses to Carlos Alcaraz and Taylor Fritz in the semifinals of the 2022 and 2024 US Open, Tiafoe highlighted his ability to empathize with his fellow American during an appearance at the ESPN desk after the match.

articles.title: LSU announces final decision on adding former NFL players
articles.summary: The biggest storyline in college football over the past few weeks has been LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin’s attempts to add multiple players to its roster who had signed NFL contracts and spent time with NFL teams this preseason. Now, LSU has made a final decision on that matter.
body: With the looming threat of expulsion from the SEC, the Tigers have made it clear that they will not add the players to the roster this season.

Heading into the 2026 season, LSU and Kiffin had been moving forward with plans to bring in at least three players who signed professional contracts this summer, including former Ole Miss players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris.

Adding those players to the roster would break two separate league rules, as the SEC prohibits players from entering the conference after signing a professional contract while also restricting intraconference transfers outside of the designated transfer portal window.

However, a Baton Rouge judge has issued an order preventing both the NCAA and SEC from enforcing their restrictions related to eligibility, the transfer portal, and professional players returning to college football.

articles.title: The SEC will vote to expel LSU. Here's why
articles.summary: Here's why originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The SEC is fed up with Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers after their debacle signing pro football players to the team.
body: To do so, a vote of two-thirds of all the presidents is required to end a school's tenure with the conference according to SEC rules. The SEC said in a statement, "The SEC and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed."
"Today's filing is necessary to defend that right and preserve the Conference's ability to govern competition among its members."

A meeting is set for Thursday, September 10 to “decide whether to terminate Louisiana State University (“LSU”) as an SEC member institution pursuant to Section 3.1.5 of the SEC Constitution and Bylaws,” per On3 Sports.

If this does not show how fed up the SEC is with Lane Kiffin and his antics, then nothing does. According to ESPN, the SEC's amended complaint mentioned Kiffin's comments after their 5110 landslide win over Clemson on Saturday; "Imagine if we had pro players." His comment shows how he neglects the ruling that players who have signed a pro contract cannot return to college.

articles.title: Tiafoe consoles tearful Michelsen after remarkable US Open comeback
articles.summary: Frances Tiafoe comes from two sets and a break down to beat Alex Michelsen in a thrilling comeback to reach the US Open semi-finals.
body: Eleventh seed Tiafoe was outplayed by world number 46 Michelsen for the first half of the match, but battled back from 5-3 down in the third set - with his opponent serving for the match - to ignite a remarkable turnaround.
In a final set of multiple breaks and swings of momentum, Tiafoe triumphed in the 10-point tie-break to win 5-7 3-6 7-5 6-3 7-6 (10-6).
Victory means 28-year-old Tiafoe reaches his third US Open semi-final in five years, where he will play defending champion Carlos Alcaraz or American eighth seed Ben Shelton.
Michelsen, 22, who was competing in his first Grand Slam quarter-final, was in tears as the pair embraced after a match which lasted four hours and 38 minutes.

articles.title: In the middle again - but Mourinho says Alexander-Arnold 'not a midfielder'
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold started in midfield for Real Madrid's win over Inter - but Jose Mourinho says it is not his best position.
body: It's the question that just doesn't seem to go away - can Trent Alexander-Arnold really work in midfield?
Gareth Southgate played him there for England during Euro 2024 before ending the experiment after only two group games.
Jurgen Klopp's entire Liverpool gameplan relied on his ability to step into the middle and spray passes around... albeit from a starting position of right-back.
And now Jose Mourinho has become the latest manager to dabble, picking the 27-year-old in midfield for Real Madrid's Champions League win over Inter Milan on Tuesday.

articles.title: Osaka's US Open fashion ensemble: Which outfit was your favourite?
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka may have exited the US Open, but she went out with a burst - of colour, and a bit of swag. Which outfit was your best of the tournament?
body: The two-time US Open champion may have lost a lopsided fourth-round match to Elena Rybakina but she continued to make her mark as the undisputed fashion queen on tour.

Osaka, already known for her walk-on fashion reveals at tournaments, has been upping her game at the year's final major with a series of dramatic ensembles - all with a basketball theme as her sponsor, Nike, honours the New York Knicks' championship win.

For her first-round match, Osaka channelled NBA great Allen Iverson in a long, white tulle skirt and a dramatic grey, hooded robe. When she removed the hood, Osaka's hair was in cornrows under a headband, recalling Iverson's look when was the NBA MVP while playing for the Philadelphia 76ers.
Her ensemble was designed by Who Decides War, the New York-based streetwear brand.
